I know "-gate" is added to things considered scandalous and I've only heard of gamer gate today, while browsing this website actually. I know it has something to do with kotaku but I'm not too sure what that is either.

I'll try to speak objectively.

About a year ago, a game developer name Zoe Quinn was found to have slept with a gaming journalist who reviewed her game, Depression Quest, and gave it high praise. This is an obvious breach of journalistic ethics. "Gamergate" emerged around the ensuing controversy.

Supporters of Gamergate insist that the movement concerns journalistic ethics, while anti-Gamergaters say it's a misogynistic movement intent on driving women out of the games industry. Several follow-up scandals to the Zoe Quinn controversy added fuel to the fire, embroiling many game developers, journalists, and critics, including perhaps the most divisive woman in gaming, Anita Sarkeesian.

The crux of the Gamergate position is that game creators are too intent on following political correctness, and are being coerced into inclusiveness by feminist ideologues (an example would be criticism The Witcher 3 received for lacking black characters, despite its setting in Polish folklore). They also believe that such ideologues are corrupting game journalism on sites from Kotaku to Wikipedia, publishing biased articles that put irrelevant social issues ahead of objectivity; and that women are perfectly welcome in the games industry, and those saying otherwise are presenting arguments in bad faith.

The crux of the anti-Gamergate position is that video games, and the tech industry in general, are hostile to women and minorities and need to be brought into the modern day. People such as Anita Sarkeesian bemoan games' fixation on violence and male power, and push for more and deeper female and minority characters in games. They have also said that Gamergate is a hate group prone to doxxing, bullying, and death threats; and that it fosters a divisive "boys club" mentality.

I encourage you to look closely and with good faith into the arguments of both sides, and their various rebuttals, before forming an opinion.

I'm quite a mentally active/creative person and I'm trying to find some ways to wind down properly. My go-tos are drawing, writing, reading or computer-based activities but it's been suggested to me that I should try other less-stimulating things. Baths bore me :(
What are some good ways to relax that are low or non-stimulating?
Try listening to a podcast. 99 Percent Invisible, The Memory Palace, Song Exploder, Radiolab, and Hello Internet are good examples.
Podcasts are not only great when your relaxing, you can get a lot done on a weekend by doing chores and just popping on a multi hour podcast (Hardcore History anyone :).
I tend to queue up Risk or Hello Internet for chores.

You could actually just sit down on a patio or whatever and look out at the world for 20 minutes and just... think. I used to do that and I accomplished a lot in the those 20 min (mentally) and I also think its important that we have time set aside each day for raw relaxation and thought.

I second this. When the weather is good I love going to a nice park, lying there in the grass and taking a short nap or just watching other people passing by. Doing nothing (physically) takes your mind to many places.

Listening to music. Really listening to it.

Lie down. Close your eyes. Pay attention to the lyrics. The choice of instruments. How the notes shape the song. Empathize with the thoughts and emotions the artist is trying to pass on to you. Songs can bring back memories or stir your imagination. All you have to do is lie there and listen.

My favorite album to do this with is Absolution, by Muse.

Listening to the whole album at once is a magnificient experience, from beggining to end, this is a masterpiece.

Never paid much attention to music until that album, it freaking hit me in the face.

To this day, whenever I feel down I listen to it and it takes me back then ;)

Meditation has been scientifically shown (like peer reviewed studies) to decrease stress, increase creativity, and generally make people happier.

I don't think it's an overnight system, but it also seems to only take a few minutes a day
My wife puts models together to unwind. I sit on the patio and zone off with a glass of scotch or listen to headphones.

Isolation float tanks as a type of meditation. You can look for floating spas in your area which, admittedly can get a little pricy but are definitely worth it. I have a hard time shutting my brain off normally and I've tried other forms of meditation but these just work for me, even if I just go once a month. I don't like baths much either but floating in absolute darkness is extremely relaxing (even if you just take a nap in there!)
